_about: Draft questions for Joshua's review. Not shown on the page until approved and copied into data/content.json. 'source' says which official text the draft is based on.

24-1016.draft: Whether trademark strength is a question of fact or law in a trademark infringement likelihood-of-confusion analysis under 15 U.S.C. § 1114.
24-1016.notes: Background paragraph dropped. Statute citation kept because it's the only place the law is identified. Edited by Joshua.

25-159.draft: When a private company uses the Natural Gas Act to seize someone's land for natural gas infrastructure, should just compensation be determined by reference to state law?
25-159.notes: Background paragraph dropped. Edited by Joshua.

25-170.source: Questions Presented, plus the question the Court added when granting
25-170.draft:
(1) Whether the Supreme Court has statutory and Article III jurisdiction to hear this case.
(2) Whether federal law precludes state-law claims seeking relief for injuries allegedly caused by the effects of interstate and international greenhouse-gas emissions on the global climate.
25-170.notes: Question 2 was added by the Court in its grant order. "This Court" changed to "the Supreme Court" so it reads clearly on its own. Edited by Joshua.

25-183.draft: Whether Title IX provides employees of federally funded educational institutions a private right of action to sue for sex discrimination in employment.
25-183.notes: Background paragraph and its case citations dropped.

25-238.source: Questions Presented (both petitions were granted on this question)
25-238.draft: Whether the Second and Fourteenth Amendments guarantee the right to possess AR-15 platform and similar semiautomatic rifles.

25-246.draft: Whether, in determining whether a fine contravenes the Excessive Fines Clause, courts may consider the gravity of the underlying offense purely in the abstract or should consider the gravity of the specific defendant's wrongdoing.
25-246.notes: Background paragraphs dropped; "The question presented is" removed.

25-352.draft: Where a defendant has filed an answer without pleading an affirmative defense, may the defendant nonetheless assert that affirmative defense as the basis for a summary judgment motion, without amending or seeking to amend its answer to plead that affirmative defense, and may a defendant do so even if an amendment adding that affirmative defense would be barred by the court's scheduling order deadline under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 16(b)(4)?
25-352.notes: Introductory sentence dropped. "Rule 16(b)(4)" now says which rules it belongs to, since the sentence naming them was dropped. Edited by Joshua.

25-417.draft: Can a federal prisoner sue prison officials for money damages under the Bivens doctrine for deliberate indifference to a non-life-threatening injury?
25-417.notes: Background paragraphs dropped; "here" removed. Edited by Joshua.

25-459.draft: Whether the phrase "goods or services from a video tape service provider," as used in the Video Privacy Protection Act's definition of "consumer," refers to all of a video tape service provider's goods or services or only to its audiovisual goods or services.

25-498.draft: Whether, for claims predicated on fund underperformance, pleading that an ERISA fiduciary failed to use the requisite "care, skill, prudence, or diligence" under the circumstances and thus breached ERISA's duty of prudence when investing plan assets requires alleging a "meaningful benchmark."
25-498.notes: Background paragraph and its citations dropped.

25-566.source: Granted on the question presented in No. 25-238
25-566.draft: Whether the Second and Fourteenth Amendments guarantee the right to possess AR-15 platform and similar semiautomatic rifles.
25-566.notes: The Court granted this petition on Viramontes's question (No. 25-238), not on this petition's own wording, so both cases show the same question.

25-579.draft:
(1) Whether the federal government's submission to a state or territorial regulator of an application to renew a permit under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) is "final agency action" that is immediately reviewable under the Administrative Procedure Act.
(2) Whether the federal government must comply with the general environmental-review procedures of the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 before submitting a permit-renewal application under RCRA, which sets forth its own specific procedures to review environmental impacts in the context of hazardous-waste treatment.
25-579.notes: Background dropped; RCRA spelled out; code citations for the APA and NEPA dropped because both laws are named. Edited by Joshua.

25-581.source: Questions Presented, limited to Questions 1 and 2
25-581.draft:
(1) Whether a law lacks general applicability under the Free Exercise Clause only if it permits unfettered discretion or categorical exemptions for comparable secular conduct.
(2) Whether the rule against excluding religious institutions from public benefits applies only to explicit government bans on participation by religious people and institutions.
25-581.notes: Background dropped. Question 3 (whether Smith should be overruled) left out because the Court did not grant it. Edited by Joshua. Question 1 uses Claude's suggested wording, approved by Joshua.

25-735.draft: Did the Veterans' Judicial Review Act strip district courts of the jurisdiction, recognized by the Supreme Court in Johnson v. Robison, to hear challenges to the constitutionality of acts of Congress affecting veterans' benefits?
25-735.notes: Case citation removed, matching the Oyez example. "This Court" changed to "the Supreme Court."

25-840.draft: Whether parents have standing to challenge a state law that requires youth shelters to notify a state child-welfare agency, rather than the parents directly, when a runaway minor seeks gender-affirming care.
25-840.notes: Background paragraphs dropped. Neutral rewording: Claude's description of the law, limited to gender-affirming care, approved by Joshua.

25-842.draft: Whether noncitizens who were "granted asylum," but whose asylum was later terminated, are eligible for adjustment to lawful permanent resident status under 8 U.S.C. § 1159(b), or are categorically ineligible.
25-842.notes: Background dropped; "LPR" spelled out; "Section 1159(b)" given its full citation since the sentence that defined it was dropped. Edited by Joshua.

25-965.draft: Whether the First Amendment's established chilling-effect doctrine—under which a credible government threat that deters the exercise of fundamental rights constitutes a complete and independently actionable constitutional injury—allows a plaintiff to bring a lawsuit based on government threats both before and after a Planning Commission meeting that chilled religious exercise, worship, and assembly, even when the city had not completed a final land-use decision.
25-965.notes: "Williamson Cnty." spelled out; dashes restored. Edited by Joshua. "county" corrected to "city" (the defendant is the City of University Heights).

25-966.source: The Court's grant order (limited to its own two questions)
25-966.draft:
(1) Whether Article III of the Constitution precludes the Department of Labor from adjudicating proceedings to collect monetary remedies from employers who have allegedly violated the terms and conditions of employment of H-2A workers and domestic workers in corresponding employment and instead requires them to be decided by a federal court.
(2) Whether 8 U.S.C. § 1188(g)(2) authorizes the Department of Labor to adjudicate such proceedings.
25-966.notes: The Court granted only its own two questions, so those replace the petition's question. Converted from all caps. Edited by Joshua.

25-1003.draft: Whether a claim relies on "a new rule of constitutional law . . . that was previously unavailable" when the habeas petitioner could have asserted a claim based on the rule in a prior federal habeas petition.
25-1003.notes: Background dropped; doubled "a" fixed. Edited by Joshua.

25-1017.draft:
(1) Does the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA) or a federal consent decree prohibit Arizona from requiring voter-registration applicants to produce "satisfactory evidence" of U.S. citizenship when registering with a state registration form?
(2) Does the NVRA prohibit Arizona from implementing a program within 90 days of a federal election to cancel the registrations of voters who are not U.S. citizens?

25-1103.draft: Whether a court may order broad discovery against an Executive Office advisory body—potentially providing much information sought on the merits of a plaintiff's Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) claims—to determine whether FOIA's disclosure requirements apply in the first place.
25-1103.notes: Background dropped; case citation removed; FOIA spelled out; "plaintiffs" corrected to "plaintiff's"; "this Court" clarified. Edited by Joshua. Question 1 (about the court of appeals' compliance with the Supreme Court's remand) dropped at Joshua's request.

25-1131.draft: Whether a land-use regulation that prohibits a religious institution from building a religious structure on its own property constitutes a "substantial burden" on religious exercise under the Substantial Burden Provision of the Religious Land Use and Institutionalized Persons Act (RLUIPA).
25-1131.notes: Question 2 (the Equal Terms Provision) left out because the Court did not grant it. Code citation dropped because the law is named.

25-1223.draft: Whether, under the Equal Access to Justice Act, "any civil action" encompasses an action seeking a writ of habeas corpus to challenge civil immigration detention.

25-1311.draft: Whether a court may hold a party in civil contempt based on a violation of an injunction's "spirit" where the injunction is silent as to the conduct upon which contempt is based; or, instead, whether a court must ground a finding of civil contempt on the violation of an order that clearly and unambiguously proscribes the precise conduct at issue.
25-1311.notes: Question 2 (the Trump v. CASA question) left out because the Court did not grant it. Edited by Joshua.

25-1343.draft: Whether material support to a terrorist organization, which makes an alien removable and ineligible for various immigration benefits—including asylum—under 8 U.S.C. § 1182(a)(3)(B)(iv)(VI), must advance the organization's actual commission of terrorism to qualify for that bar.
25-1343.notes: The official question refers to "such support" defined in the sentence before it, so that sentence's substance is folded in. "(Vl)" typo corrected to "(VI)". Lightest-touch rewrite in the set; worth a careful look. Edited by Joshua.

25-1349.draft: Does the Uniformed Services Former Spouses' Protection Act require state courts to refuse enforcement of indemnification provisions in divorce settlement agreements?

25-5343.source: The Court's grant order (limited to its own question)
25-5343.draft: Whether Stinson v. United States still correctly states the rule for the deference that courts must give the commentary to the Sentencing Guidelines.
25-5343.notes: The Court granted only its own reworded version of the petition's second question. Case citation removed.

25-5930.source: The Court's grant order (limited to its own question)
25-5930.draft: Whether a claim regarding application of time credits under the First Step Act of 2018, seeking accelerated transfer to a halfway house or home confinement, can be brought in a habeas petition under 28 U.S.C. § 2241.
25-5930.notes: The Court granted only its own question. Statutes at Large and code citations for the First Step Act dropped because the law is named; § 2241 kept because it's the only identifier for the habeas statute.

25-6623.draft: Whether the Sixth and Fourteenth Amendments guarantee a defendant charged with a serious felony the right to a trial by a 12-person jury.
25-6623.notes: The petition's request to hold the case for two other petitions dropped. Edited by Joshua.

25-7026.draft: Whether an appeals court must grant a petitioner permission to appeal under 28 U.S.C. § 2253 where the petitioner's argument has been foreclosed by binding circuit precedent but has been resolved in the petitioner's favor by another circuit.

26-12.source: The Court's grant order (limited to its own question)
26-12.draft: Whether a plaintiff challenging a facially neutral admissions policy as racially discriminatory must establish that the targeted racial group suffered an aggregate disparate impact relative to its share of the applicant pool.
26-12.notes: The Court granted only its own reworded question. Converted from all caps.

26-104.draft: Whether 8 U.S.C. § 1225(b)(2)(A) mandates the detention pending removal proceedings of aliens who, like the respondent, are present in the United States without having been admitted.

26-204.draft: Whether the federal ban on distilling spirits in a home, or in a shed or yard connected to a home, is a valid use of Congress's taxing power and the Necessary and Proper Clause.
26-204.notes: Background dropped; code citation dropped and "federal" added so the law is still identified. Plain-language rewrite by Claude, approved by Joshua.

26-426.draft:
(1) Whether the district court had jurisdiction over the respondents' claims.
(2) Whether the district court had authority to enter classwide declaratory relief and vacatur under the Administrative Procedure Act, given 8 U.S.C. § 1252(f)(1).
(3) Whether the government's guidance on third-country removals is unlawful under 8 U.S.C. § 1231(b), the Due Process Clause, or the Foreign Affairs Reform and Restructuring Act and Convention Against Torture and their implementing regulations.
26-426.notes: The Court set these questions itself. Its fourth item ("such other questions that the Government determines are appropriate") is left out because it isn't a question. Acronyms spelled out. "APA vacatur under § 1252(f)(1)" lightly reworded; worth a careful look.
26-426.status: held by Joshua: compare with how others summarize the case
